interactables.text: The Movie Star, [Vivienne Vale], is draped across the chaise in full mourning couture. She points at you with a tissue. 'You. You have KIND eyes. Not like the rest of these vultures.'

topics.text: 'He was HERE, darling. I heard him at [8:00 PM], on the dot - I was mid-affirmation.' She dabs one eye, careful of the mascara. 'I would know that screech anywhere. It said: Vivienne. I am ALIVE. And possibly: garbage slop.'

topics.prompt: Paw gently at the empty cage
topics.text: 'Do NOT touch the crime scene, darling.' She sweeps you up and holds you like a press photo. 'Rudebeak is family. Rude, loud family with a [vocabulary problem] - which is the maid's doing, by the way. Rosa taught him THAT phrase. I keep a list.'

topics.prompt: Bat the little speaker out where she can see it
topics.text: She stares at it for a long moment. Something sharpens behind the movie-star eyes. 'That is not mine. That is not RUDEBEAK'S.' Then, quieter: 'The [film people] wire everything, you know. There are cables in my walls I have never been introduced to.'

interactables.text: The Bird Handler, [Petra], sits perfectly still beside an untouched bowl of seed, the way professionals wait. She gives you a nod, one working animal expert to another.

topics.text: 'His six o'clock snack. [He never misses it]. Never.' Her voice is flat and certain, a metronome of worry. 'Whatever happened, by six o'clock he was already somewhere he could not smell this bowl.'

topics.prompt: Tilt your head at her, professionally
topics.text: 'You want the profile? Blue-and-gold macaw, nineteen years old, ego like a co-star, lungs like a fire alarm.' She almost smiles. 'Loud in daylight. But put him somewhere [dark and quiet] and he goes silent as a stone. Handler trick. Works every time.'

topics.prompt: Report the garden feathers with a slow blink
topics.text: You aim a long, deliberate blink toward the garden. She reads you perfectly. 'The bird bath. Of course - he loves that thing.' Her jaw sets. 'Understand something, cat. [Wet feathers mean a happy bird]. A happy bird does not fly away from his own bath. Someone picked him up. He only allows that when he is soggy and smug.'

interactables.text: The [Empty Cage]. The latch is [snapped clean off]. The seed tray is bone dry, and the feathers under the cage have settled flat.
Tucked behind the cage stand, half-hidden by a fern: a small [Wireless Speaker]. A thin [Audio Cable] trails behind the furniture toward the wall.
A film crew camera on a tripod. The red light says [Recording]. It's been on all day. Someone forgot to check if it was aimed at the [cage].
A booklet: 'Phrases We've Taught Rudebeak.' Entries include: 'Hello gorgeous', 'Oscar worthy', and '[Garbage slop]' - the last one furiously crossed out and labeled: '[Maid's fault]'.

localDeductionSentence: Everyone heard the [8:00 PM Squawk] - but the [Broken Latch] and the [Hidden Speaker] under the cage tell a very different story.
